title: Bases and coordinates

review.history: source gap; no origin or priority assertions

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Keep a point fixed while changing the directions used to describe it.
meaning: A basis is an independent spanning collection. An ordered basis gives a vector one unique list of coefficients. In the plane, two independent arrows can be tilted, stretched or reversed and still describe every target. A dependent pair loses that unique coordinate description.

definition.setting: Real vector spaces with an explicit two-dimensional coordinate model.

signature.a,b,c,d: Candidate direction columns u=(a,c), v=(b,d), entries in [-2,2].
signature.r,s: Unique basis coefficients only when the candidate pair is independent and finite arithmetic can represent the result; otherwise null.
signature.determinant: ad-bc; nonzero exactly when this pair is a basis of R².
signature.rank,basisKind: Rank 2/1/0 and plane/line/zero span classification of the candidate columns.
signature.solutionStatus: unique, infinite_solutions, no_solution or numeric_range; valid mathematical configurations need not have unique coordinates.

conditions: The ordered candidate directions are u=(a,c) and v=(b,d), the columns of B=[[a,b],[c,d]].
The pair is a basis of R² exactly when det(B)=ad-bc is nonzero; it need not be perpendicular or have unit length.
For a nonzero determinant, each target (x,y) has one coefficient pair (r,s) satisfying r*u+s*v=(x,y).
A dependent pair is valid model input but is not a basis of the plane. Its target equation can have infinitely many solutions or no solution.
Physical coordinates use one compatible coordinate system and units; basis coefficients describe multiples of the declared directions.
definition.domain_notes: The general notion of a basis applies to vector spaces and subspaces beyond the real plane. This live model tests exactly two ordered real plane directions and a target vector, with bounded entries and target components. The coefficient results are not artificially restricted to the slider bounds and can grow large near dependence. The bounded control box is not itself a vector space. The exact zero determinant case is classified separately from a nearby nonzero determinant; finite-precision numerical range can still prevent a displayed unique result. No arbitrary-dimension solver or full change-of-basis matrix between two arbitrary bases is implemented.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: determinant=a*d-b*c. If determinant!=0, output=r=(d*x-b*y)/determinant and s=(a*y-c*x)/determinant; reconstruct (a*r+b*s,c*r+d*s). If determinant=0, output/r/s are null and the model distinguishes infinite_solutions from no_solution. rank is 2 for nonzero determinant, 1 for a nonzero dependent pair, otherwise 0. Nonfinite computed coordinates use solutionStatus=numeric_range, not fabricated finite coefficients.
grammar.precedence: Scale components before adding. Matrix products act on column vectors from right to left; an ordered pair retains its stated coordinate order.

grammar.ast_coverage: The AST explicitly computes the determinant and both quotient formulas, then constructs the ordered coefficient pair. Its declared domain is the unique branch det(B)!=0. The total interactive model also classifies dependent configurations without evaluating those division nodes; null means no unique coordinates, not the zero vector. Rank and consistency classification are stated model metadata outside this arithmetic tree.

properties.claim: A basis gives unique coefficients for each vector in its space.
properties.conditions: The candidate vectors span the space and are linearly independent.
properties.derivation: Existence comes from spanning. If two coefficient lists gave the same vector, subtracting them would give a zero linear combination; independence forces every difference coefficient to be zero.
properties.status: definition-level reference and author explanation; independent review pending

properties.claim: A dependent pair can have reachable targets without unique coefficients and other targets that are unreachable.
properties.conditions: Two dependent columns in the real plane.
properties.derivation: The columns span at most one line. On that span, a nonzero dependence can be added to any solution; off that span, no solution exists.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

prompts.prompt: Must a basis be perpendicular or made of unit arrows?
prompts.answer: No. Independence and spanning are the requirements; length and angle can vary.

prompts.prompt: Does determinant zero mean every target has no solution?
prompts.answer: No. Targets in the column span have infinitely many coefficient pairs; targets outside it have no solution.
